कम्पनियों के नाम कम्पनी रजिस्टर से इस आधार पर नाम हटाने का आवेदन प्राप्त हुआ है कि कम्पनी के निगमन के एक वर्ष के भीतर कारोबार 
आरंभ करने में विफल रहे हैं या इस आधार पर कि कम्पनी पूर्ववर्ती 2 वित्तीय वर्षों से कारोबार नहीं कर पाई है और इस अवधि के भीतर कम्पनी 
अधिनियम, 2013 की धारा 455 के तहत निष्क्रिय कम्पनी की स्थिति प्राप्त करने का आदेश का आवेदन नहीं किया है या कम्पनी ने निष्क्रिय 
कम्पनी की स्थिति प्राप्त कर ली है, पर वे कम्पनी के रूप में पंजीकरण नहीं रखना चाहते और अतः कम्पनी रजिस्ट्रार से अपना/अपने नाम हटाने 
का अनुरोध किया है। 

3. तदनुसार, कम्पनी रजिस्ट्रार उपर्युक्त कम्पनियों के नामों को कम्पनियों के रजिस्टर से हटाने का प्रस्ताव करता है। 

4. यदि किसी व्यक्ति/संस्था को कम्पनी को कम्पनी रजिस्ट्रार से कम्पनियों का नाम हटाने के प्रस्ताव से आपत्ति है तो वह व्यक्ति/संस्था 
इस सूचना के प्रकाशन की तारीख से 30 (तीस) दिनों के भीतर उपर्युक्त कार्यालय के पते पर अपनी आपत्ति भेज सकते हैं |

कम्पनियों के नाम कम्पनी रजिस्टर से इस आधार पर नाम हटाने का आवेदन प्राप्त हुआ है कि कम्पनी के निगमन के एक वर्ष के भीतर कारोबार 
आरंभ करने में विफल रहे हैं या इस आधार पर कि कम्पनी पूर्ववर्ती 2 वित्तीय वर्षों से कारोबार नहीं कर पाई है और इस अवधि के भीतर कम्पनी 
अधिनियम, 2013 की धारा 455 के तहत निष्क्रिय कम्पनी की स्थिति प्राप्त करने का आदेश का आवेदन नहीं किया है या कम्पनी ने निष्क्रिय 
कम्पनी की स्थिति प्राप्त कर ली है, पर वे कम्पनी के रूप में पंजीकरण नहीं रखना चाहते और अतः कम्पनी रजिस्ट्रार से अपना/अपने नाम हटाने

2. इसके द्वारा यह सूचित किया जाता है कि कम्पनी अधिनियम, 2013 की धारा 248 (2) के तहत कम्पनी रजिस्ट्रार को उपर्युक्त 
कम्पनियों के नाम कम्पनी रजिस्टर से इस आधार पर नाम हटाने का आवेदन प्राप्त हुआ है कि कम्पनी के निगमन के एक वर्ष के भीतर कारोबार 
आरंभ करने में विफल रहे हैं या इस आधार पर कि कम्पनी पूर्ववर्ती 2 वित्तीय वर्षों से कारोबार नहीं कर पाई है और इस अवधि के भीतर कम्पनी 
अधिनियम, 2013 की धारा 455 के तहत निष्क्रिय कम्पनी की स्थिति प्राप्त करने का आदेश का आवेदन नहीं किया है या कम्पनी ने निष्क्रिय 
कम्पनी की स्थिति प्राप्त कर ली है, पर वे कम्पनी के रूप में पंजीकरण नहीं रखना चाहते और अतः कम्पनी रजिस्ट्रार से अपना/अपने नाम हटाने 
का अनुरोध किया है। 


3. तदनुसार, कम्पनी रजिस्ट्रार उपर्युक्त कम्पनियों के नामों को कम्पनियों के रजिस्टर से हटाने का प्रस्ताव करता है। 


4. यदि किसी व्यक्ति/संस्था को कम्पनी को कम्पनी रजिस्ट्रार से कम्पनियों का नाम हटाने के प्रस्ताव से आपत्ति है तो वह व्यक्ति/संस्था 
इस सूचना के प्रकाशन की तारीख से 30 (तीस) दिनों के भीतर उपर्युक्त कार्यालय के पते पर अपनी आपत्ति भेज सकते हैं |

आरंभ करने में विफल रहे हैं या इस आधार पर कि कम्पनी पूर्ववर्ती 2 वित्तीय वर्षों से कारोबार नहीं कर पाई है और इस अवधि के भीतर कम्पनी 
अधिनियम, 2013 की धारा 455 के तहत निष्क्रिय कम्पनी की स्थिति प्राप्त करने का आदेश का आवेदन नहीं किया है या कम्पनी ने निष्क्रिय 
कम्पनी की स्थिति प्राप्त कर ली है, पर वे कम्पनी के रूप में पंजीकरण नहीं रखना चाहते और अतः कम्पनी रजिस्ट्रार से अपना/अपने नाम हटाने 
का अनुरोध किया है। 


3. तदनुसार, कम्पनी रजिस्ट्रार उपर्युक्त कम्पनियों के नामों को कम्पनियों के रजिस्टर से हटाने का प्रस्ताव करता है। 


4. यदि किसी व्यक्ति/संस्था को कम्पनी को कम्पनी रजिस्ट्रार से कम्पनियों का नाम हटाने के प्रस्ताव से आपत्ति है तो वह व्यक्ति/संस्था

कम्पनियों के नाम कम्पनी रजिस्टर से इस आधार पर नाम हटाने का आवेदन प्राप्त हुआ है कि कम्पनी के निगमन के एक वर्ष के भीतर कारोबार 
आरंभ करने में विफल रहे हैं या इस आधार पर कि कम्पनी पूर्ववर्ती 2 वित्तीय वर्षों से कारोबार नहीं कर पाई है और इस अवधि के भीतर कम्पनी 
अधिनियम, 2013 की धारा 455 के तहत निष्क्रिय कम्पनी की स्थिति प्राप्त करने का आदेश का आवेदन नहीं किया है या कम्पनी ने निष्क्रिय 
कम्पनी की स्थिति प्राप्त कर ली है, पर वे कम्पनी के रूप में पंजीकरण नहीं रखना चाहते और अतः कम्पनी रजिस्ट्रार से अपना/अपने नाम हटाने 
का अनुरोध किया है। 

3. तदनुसार, कम्पनी रजिस्ट्रार उपर्युक्त कम्पनियों के नामों को कम्पनियों के रजिस्टर से हटाने का प्रस्ताव करता है। 


4. यदि किसी व्यक्ति/संस्था को कम्पनी को कम्पनी रजिस्ट्रार से कम्पनियों का नाम हटाने के प्रस्ताव से आपत्ति है तो वह व्यक्ति/संस्था 
इस सूचना के प्रकाशन की तारीख से 30 (तीस) दिनों के भीतर उपर्युक्त कार्यालय के पते पर अपनी आपत्ति भेज सकते हैं |

कम्पनियों के नाम कम्पनी रजिस्टर से इस आधार पर नाम हटाने का आवेदन प्राप्त हुआ है कि कम्पनी के निगमन के एक वर्ष के भीतर कारोबार

कम्पनियों के नाम कम्पनी रजिस्टर से इस आधार पर नाम हटाने का आवेदन प्राप्त हुआ है कि कम्पनी के निगमन के एक वर्ष के भीतर कारोबार 
आरंभ करने में विफल रहे हैं या इस आधार पर कि कम्पनी पूर्ववर्ती 2 वित्तीय वर्षों से कारोबार नहीं कर पाई है और इस अवधि के भीतर कम्पनी 
अधिनियम, 2013 की धारा 455 के तहत निष्क्रिय कम्पनी की स्थिति प्राप्त करने का आदेश का आवेदन नहीं किया है या कम्पनी ने निष्क्रिय 
कम्पनी की स्थिति प्राप्त कर ली है, पर वे कम्पनी के रूप में पंजीकरण नहीं रखना चाहते और अतः कम्पनी रजिस्ट्रार से अपना/अपने नाम हटाने

4. यदि किसी व्यक्ति/संस्था को कम्पनी को कम्पनी रजिस्ट्रार से कम्पनियों का नाम हटाने के प्रस्ताव से आपत्ति है तो वह व्यक्ति/संस्था

less than the number of non-independent directors to constitute the quorum for the meeting of the Board of Directors. 


Any Director participating through Electronic Mode in respect of restricted items with the express permission of Chairman 
shall however, neither be entitled to vote nor be counted for the purpose of Quorum in respect of such restricted items. 


Quorum shall be present throughout the Meeting. Quorum shall be present not only at the time of commencement of the 
Meeting but also while transacting business. 


For the purpose of this Article:- 


(1) "total strength" means the total strength of the Directors of the Company as determined in pursuance of the Act, after 
deducting there from the number of the Directors, if any, whose place may be vacant at the time; 


(2) "interested Director" means any Director whose presence cannot by reason of Article 136 or any other provision in the 
Act count for the purpose of forming a quorum at a meeting of the Board, at the time of the discussion or vote on any matter.

का.आ. 1752.--केन्द्रीय सरकार को यह प्रतीत होता है कि सार्वजनिक हित में परिवहन के लिए आंध्रप्रदेश राज्य 
के डॉ. बी.आर. अम्बेडकर कोनासीमा जिले में निर्दिष्ट भूमि के माध्यम से आई. एम. सी. लिमिटेड द्वारा काकीनाडा- 
विजयवाड़ा-नेल्लोर (के.वी.एन.पी.एल.) तक प्राकृतिक गैस पाइपलाइन बिछाई जानी चाहिए; 
और केन्द्रीय सरकार को ऐसा प्रतीत होता है कि ऐसी पाइपलाइन बिछाने के प्रयोजन के लिए, इस अधिसूचना के 
साथ संलग्न अनुसूची में वर्णित भूमि में उपयोगकर्ता का अधिकार प्राप्त करना आवश्यक है; 


3928 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : NOVEMBER 11, 2023/KARTIKA 20, 1945 


[PART II—SEC. 3(ii)] 


अत: अब, केन्द्रीय सरकार, पेट्रोलियम और खनिज पाइपलाइन (भूमि A उपयोगकर्ता के अधिकार का Asta) 
अधिनियम, 1962 (1962 का 50) की धारा 3 की उपधारा (1) द्वारा प्रदत्त शक्तियों का प्रयोग करते हुए, उस भूमि में 
उपयोग के अधिकार का अर्जन करने के अपने आशय की घोषणा करती है ; 


उक्त अनुसूची में वर्णित भूमि में रुचि रखनेवाला कोई भी व्यक्ति भारत के राजपत्र में प्रकाशित इस असाधारण 
अधिसूचना की प्रतियाँ आम जनता को उपलब्ध कराने की दिनांक से 21 दिनों के भीतर लिखित रूप में अधिग्रहण पर 


आपत्ति जता सकता है, उसमें उपयोगकर्ता के अधिकार या भूमि के नीचे पाइपलाइन बिछाने का अधिकार सक्षम अधिकारी 
को, सक्षम अधिकारी, आई. एम. सी. लिमिटेड, काकीनाडा-विजयवाड़ा-नेल्लोर प्राकृतिक गैस पाइपलाइन परियोजना, 
क.नं. 66-9-2/1, पहली मंजिल, कमलेंद्रनाथ स्ट्रीट, नरसच्ना नगर, काकीनाडा- 533003, आंध्रप्रदेश में भेज सकेगा।

का.आ. 1753.--पेट्रोलियम और खनिज पाइपलाइन (भूमि में प्रयोक्ता के अधिकार का अर्जन) अधिनियम, 
1962 (1962 का 50) (इसमें इसके बाद उक्त अधिनियम कहा गया है) की धारा 2 के खंड (क) के अनुसरण में भारत सरकार 
एतदद्वारा, झारखंड राज्य में मैसर्स गेल (इंडिया) लिमिटेड की सभी प्राकृतिक गैस पाइपलाइन परियोजनाओं के लिए 
पेट्रोलियम और खनिज पाइपलाइन (भूमि में प्रयोक्ता के अधिकार का अर्जन) अधिनियम, 1962 के तहत श्री बीर प्रकाश 
प्रसाद, उप समाहर्ता (सेवानिवृत्त), झारखंड राज्य प्रशासनिक सेवा को, प्रतिनियुक्ति के आधार पर, सक्षम प्राधिकारी के 
कार्यो का निर्वहन करने के लिये प्राधिकृत करती है। 


2. झारखंड राज्य में मैसर्स गेल (इंडिया) लिमिटेड के लिए दिनांक 12.08.2022 को भारत के असाधारण राजपत्र में 
प्रकाशित दिनांक 10.08.2022 की अधिसूचना संख्या सां.आ. 3802(अ) द्वारा पूर्व में अधिसूचित सक्षम प्राधिकारी, 
श्रीमती नुपुर नलिनी भगत, सहायक बंदोबस्त अधिकारी, रांची, झारखंड सरकार को निरस्त किया जाता है| 


3. यह अधिसूचना इसके जारी होने की तिथि से प्रभावी होगी।

का.आ. 1754.--भारत सरकार ने पेट्रोलियम और खनिज पाइपलाइन (भूमि में उपयोग के अधिकार का अर्जन) 
अधिनियम, 1962 (1962 का 50) (जिसे इसमें इसके पश्चात उक्त अधिनियम कहा गया है) की धारा 3 की उपधारा (1) के 
अधीन जारी भारत सरकार के पेट्रोलियम और प्राकृतिक गैस मंत्रालय की अधिसूचना संख्या का.आ. 1608 (अ) क्रमशः दिनांक 
28.03.2023 उस अधिसूचना से संलग्न अनुसूची में विनिर्दिष्ट भूमि में गेल (इण्डिया) लिमिटेड द्वारा पश्चिम बंगाल राज्य में 
जगदीशपुर-हल्दिया - बोकारो- धामरा पाइपलाइन (जे एच बी डी पी एल) और eae पाइपलाइन के माध्यम से प्राकृ 


तिक गैस के परिवहन के लिए पाइप लाइन बिछाने के प्रयोजन के लिए उपयोग के अधिकार का अर्जन करने के अपने आशय 
की घोषणा की थी; 


और उक्त राजपत्रित अधिसूचना की प्रतियां जनता को उपलब्ध करा दी गई थी; 


और, सक्षम प्राधिकार ने, उक्त अधिनियम की धारा 6 की उप-धारा (1) के अधीन भारत सरकार को अपनी रिपोर्ट दे 
दी है; 


और भारत सरकार ने, उक्त रिपोर्ट पर विचार करने के पश्चात और यह संतुष्ट हो जाने पर कि उक्त भूमि पाइपलाइनें 
बिछाने के लिए अपेक्षित है, उस में उपयोग के अधिकार का अर्जन करने का विनिश्चय किया है; 


अतः अब, भारत सरकार, उक्त अधिनियम की धारा 6 की उप-धारा (1) द्वारा wart शक्तियों का प्रयोग करते हुये, 
यह घोषणा करती है कि इस अधिसूचना से संलग्न अनुसूची में विनिर्दिष्ट भूमि में पाइपलाइनें बिछाने के लिए उपयोग के 
अधिकार का अर्जन किया जाता है; 


और भारत सरकार, उक्त अधिनियम कि धारा 6 कि उप-धारा (4) द्वारा प्रदत्त शक्तियों का प्रयोग करते हुये, निर्देश 
देती है कि पाइपलाइनें बिछाने के लिए भूमि में उपयोग का अधिकार, इस घोषणा के प्रकाशन की तारीख को, भारत सरकार 
में निहित होने के बजाए, पाइपलाइनें बिछाने का प्रस्ताव करने वाली गेल (इण्डिया) लिमिटेड में निहित होगा और तदुपरि, भूमि 
में ऐसे उपयोग का अधिकार, इस प्रकार अधिरोपित निबंधनों और शर्तों के अधीन रहते हुये, सभी विल्लंगमों से मुक्त, गेल

dispute existing between the employers in relation to the Management of Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd., and

Employees Union under Clause (d) of Sub-Section (1) and Sub-Section (2A) of Section 10 of the Industrial Dispute 
Act, 1947 (14 of 1947) vide their order No. L-30011/11/2016-IR(M) dated 13.6.2016 to this Tribunal for adjudication 
to the following effect. 


SCHEDULE 


“Whether the demand of the union to bear the expenditure on labour cost by the management 
of Khurda LPG Plant of M/s BPCL towards running the canteen in the establishment in stead of 
revising the canteen subsidy amount to Rs. 1600/- p.m. per employee is legal and/or justified. If so, 
what relief the employees of the union are entitled to?” 


2: After receipt of the schedule of reference and the Statement of Claim filed by the 27 Party-Union notice was 
issued to the 1“ Party-Managements for filing of their Written Statements to which the 1“ Party-Managements have 
duly filed during course of adjudication. 


3. The 211 Party-Union in its Statement of Claim has raised objections against the introduction of canteen 
cafeteria facility instead of the practice of canteen subsidy extended to the regular employees of the Management at 
its LPG Plant, Khurda and prayed to declare the action of the Management as illegal and violative of applicable 
statutes / law, etc. 


4. On the other hand, the 1“ Party-Managements in their Written Statement inter-alia have tried to justify their 
action of introducing the provisions of canteen cafeteria facility in place of the existing canteen subsidy extended to 
the regular employees at their LPG Plant, Khurda and denied all the allegations made by the 2™ Party-Union in their 
Statement of Claim. 


Ds However, during the course of adjudication, both the parties have settled the present dispute out of court and 
filed original copy of their Memorandum of Settlement in Form — H containing 02 (two) numbers of terms and 
conditions as agreed between them in this dispute. Submitting their Memorandum of Settlement, both parties have 
prayed the Tribunal to close this case in terms of the settlement arrived at between them. The terms of Memorandum 
of Settlement executed between Shri Girish Sonawane, Territory Manager (LPG), M/s. BPCL, Khurda and Shri 
Ramesh Nayak, Authorised Representative of the 27 Party-Union are as under. 


“1, That pursuant to the execution of agreement on wages and other matters with 1“ party M/s. Bharat 
Petroleum Corporation Ltd on 28.3.2023, the 270 party has settled the disputes with the Management under 
the settlement and accordingly the 2" party union does not want to proceed further with the present case. 


2. That it is further agreed between the parties to submit the Memorandum of Settlement before the 
Presiding Officer, Central Govt. Labour Court, Bhubaneswar in I.D. Case No. 35 of 2016 as a measure of 
mutual settlement.” 


6. Considering the facts and circumstance and the submissions of the stake holders of this case, the Tribunal is 
of the opinion that whatever dispute was existing between the 1“ Party-Management and the 2" Party-Union, the 
same have already been settled and no further adjudication is required under the Act. Hence this award is passed in 
terms of the Memorandum of Settlement arrived at between the 1“ Party-Management and the 27 Party-Union. The 
Memorandum of Settlement filed by the parties in this case forms part of the award. 


7. This is the award of this Tribunal.

AWARD 


By order No. L-31011/7/2006 (IR(B-II)) dated 13.09.2006, the Central Government, Ministry of Labour in 
exercise of the power conferred under section 10(1)(d) and (2A) of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 has referred the 
following issues to this Tribunal for adjudication. 


“Whether the action of the management of M/s. ATC (Clearing & Shipping) Pvt. Ltd., Mumbai in imposing 
the punishment of dismissal from services of Shri Jeevan Pawar w.e.f. 21.10.2005 is justified? If not, what relief the 
workman Shri Jeevan Pawar is entitled to?” 


The facts giving rise to the reference in brief are that the concerned workman was appointed as Clerk in the 
establishment of M/s. ATC (Clearing & Shipping) Pvt. Ltd., Mumbai in the year 1981. In due course, he was 
promoted as a Sr. Clerk. 


That sometime in the year 2005, he was placed under suspension for committing misconduct of 
misappropriation of the funds of the Company. Later, he was charge sheeted for committing misconduct under clause 
22(a), 22(d) and 22(i) of Model Standing Order framed under the Industrial Employment Standing Order Act, 1946 
on 24.03.2005 i.e. for inflating bills of mobile phone sets worth Rs.5,800/- and Rs.7150/- as Rs.15,800/- and 
Rs.17,150/-, purchased for official use from Coral Trading Company and M/s. Om Sai Electronics and Gift Articles, 
Santacruz and thereby misappropriating a sum of Rs.20,000/- and which was corroborated by Mr. Salim & Mr. Javed, 
the suppliers of those two mobile sets. 


4042 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : NOVEMBER 11, 2023/KARTIKA 20, 1945 [PART II—SEC. 3(ii)] 


Then management initiated departmental enquiry on such charges against the concerned workman. The 
concerned workman fully participated in the domestic enquiry. Inquiry Officer considering both oral and 
documentary evidence which were produced before him, found the concerned workman guilty to the charges. The 
disciplinary authority concurring with the finding of the Inquiry Officer proposed punishment of ‘removal from 
service’. Accordingly, the concerned workman was terminated from the services w.e.f. 21.10.2005. 


Challenging the order of dismissal of service, the concerned workman raised an industrial dispute before the 
appropriate authority and who in turn referred the matter to this tribunal for adjudication. 


Record shows the predecessor of this tribunal passed a preliminary award on 01.02.2013 holding the 
domestic enquiry conducted by the employer / management of M/s. ATC (Clearing & Shipping) Pvt. Ltd., Mumbai 
against the concerned workman not to be fair and proper and findings given by the Inquiry Officer to be totally 
perverse. Therefore, in view of provisions of section 11A of the I.D. Act, extended the management / employer to 
prove the charge against the concerned workman by adducing further evidence. 


The management / employer challenged the preliminary award dated 01.02.2013 before the Hon’ble High 
Court of Bombay and filed the writ petition No. 7386 / 2013. The Hon’ble High Court of Bombay affirmed the 
preliminary award dated 01.02.2013 and dismissed the writ petition. 


The management in order to prove the charge which it has brought against the concerned workman for 
misappropriation of Rs.20,000/- by inflating the bills of two mobile sets examined its following officials / staff:- 


1. Shri Prashant Sharad Moghe, its Manager who was working as Dy. Manager [A/cs. Dept.] in the year 2005, 
2 Shri Girish Achut Gadre, Chief Manager [A/cs.], 

3. Shri Ganesh Narayan Karandikar, Head of Export Dept. of the management and 

4 Shri Arvind Krishanji Kunte, ex-employee of the company. 


Now, let me see whether the management of the employer has been able to prove the charge that has been 
brought against the concerned workman. 


The charge sheet dated 24.03.2005 shows that while conducting statutory audit by M/s. H.T. Patel and 
Company, Chartered Accountant engaged by the employer for the financial year 2004 — 2005, it was found certain 
mobile phones were purchased for use of the staff and for making gift to the guest of the organization and bills raised 
to be doubtful. On queries, it was reported by Shri Prashant Sharad Moghe that a mobile set worth Rs.15,800/- was 
purchased by the company for use of Mr. Somesh Vaidya, Custom Clerk and invoice for the purchase of such mobile 
was sanctioned by Mr. Navroz, Administrative Manager. Mr. Navroz on queries informed Mr. Moghe mobile set 
worth Rs.5,800/- was actually purchased for use of Mr. S. Vaidya. It was found that said mobile phone was purchased 
from M/s. Coral Trading Company vide Invoice No. 93 EB. 


It has been alleged in the charge sheet, the concerned workman was the one who wrote the price of mobile 
set as Rs.15,800/- in place of Rs.5,800/- and wrote and drew a cheque worth Rs.15,800/- in favour of M/s. Coral 
Trading Company. That management called Mr. Salim and Mr. Javed two representatives of M/s. Coral Trading 
Company to clarify on the matter and who informed Mr. Navroz, that they were influenced by the concerned 
workman to alter the amount by adding certain figures on invoice. Mr. Javed furnished a written statement to that 
effect before Mr. A.K. Kunte, Dy. Manager of the company on 25.02.2005. 


It further shows that another mobile phone set of Nokia was purchased from M/s. Om Sai Electronics and 
Gift Articles, situated at 212, Hanuman Bldg., Vakola, Santacruz [East], Mumbai — 400 055. The said set was 
supplied by Mr. Javed and Mr. Salim through bill No. 394 dated 09.04.2004. The actual price of the said set was 
Rs.7150/- but the concerned workman by influencing Mr. Salim and Mr. Javed altered the bill for Rs.17,150/- and 
managed to issue cheque No. 673059 dated 19.10.2004 drawn on Corporation Bank, Fort branch and thereby 
managed to misappropriate Rs.10,000/- by influencing Mr. Salim and Mr. Javed. 


Therefore, the management considering the above conduct of the concerned workman to be grave in nature 
causing financial loss to the establishment by practicing fraud for his own financial gain charge sheeted him under 
clause 22 (a), 22(d) and 220) of Model Standing Order, framed under the Industrial Employment Standing Order 
Act, 1946 on 24.03.2005. 


Shri Prashant Sharad Moghe in his evidence in chief on affidavit stated that being Dy. Management [A/cs. 
Dept.] he used to work as an Internal Auditor though the company had engaged M/s. H.T. Patel & Co. Chartered 
Accountant as its statutory auditor. That during the internal audit and on scrutiny of mobile purchased bills, he found 
Bill No. 394:93EV:50:46A doubtful as amount mentioned in those bills being altered. He has further stated that the 
amount mentioned in those 4 bills was much more than the actual price of purchased mobile phone sets. He has also 
stated that different pens with different colours of ink being used in the preparation of those 4 bills. He found that 
figure ‘1’ being written in different colour of ink in those bills. He questioned Shri Ganesh Narayan Karandikar and 


[भाग तर---खण्ड 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : नवम्बर 11, 2023/कार्तिक 20, 1945 4043 


Mr. Navroz Langrana, the two persons who had sanctioned and approved those bills and who have stated alteration in 
those two bills. 


He has stated that he was informed by Mr. Navroz Langrana that he sanctioned bill for Rs.5,800/- and not for 
Rs.15,800/- against the purchase of mobile set. Then he submitted his Internal Audit Report to Shri Girish Achut 
Gadre, Chief Manager [A/cs.] for further action along with copies of bills. 


He has also stated that at the relevant time the concerned workman Shri Jeevan Pawar was working as a 
Sr. Clerk in A/cs. Dept. and who has to make entries of the approved bills in the books of accounts and based on 
which payments used to be released. It was the duty of Mr. Jeevan Pawar to issue cheques to the parties after 
approval. 


But, during cross examination, he has admitted that during the internal audit he did not notice any 
discrepancy in the bills before the statutory audit. He was unable to say the models and price of those mobile phones 
that were purchased under those two disputed bills. 


He further admitted that no charge was brought against the concerned workman for over writing or causing 
alteration in the bills. That he is not a hand writing expert and he has no authority to certify the difference of colour in 
the ink. He has also admitted that when he examined those disputed bills, the amounts on the disputed bills were 
written in words. There was no discrepancy in the amounts written in figures and in words in those disputed bills. He 
has also admitted in his internal audit report submitted before Shri Girish Achut Gadre, he did not brought any 
allegation against the concerned workman for alteration in those disputed bills. 


Therefore, such evidence of Shri Prashant Sharad Moghe made during cross examination totally discredit 
what he has stated against the concerned workman in his evidence in chief on affidavit. Infact, his admission creates a 
doubt about the allegations and charge that have been brought against the concerned workman and prove the charges 
that have been brought against the concerned workman was / is not proper and supported by any documentary 
evidence. 


Similarly, Shri Girish Achut Gadre, Chief Manager [A/cs.] in his evidence in chief has stated that on 
receiving report from Shri Prashant Sharad Moghe Dy. Manager [A/cs.], he called for comments from Shri Ganesh 
Narayan Karandikar and Mr. Navroz Langrana about the discrepancy in the disputed bills which they had sanctioned 
and approved. He has stated that Mr. Navroz Langrana used to verify the product with the bills and used to hand over 
the set to the concerned workman for whom the mobile phone was ordered. He has also stated that Mr. Navroz 
Langrana informed him many times the column meant for mentioning amounts in words in the invoice / bill used to 
be left blank as price mentioned on the mobile cover box used to match with the amount mentioned in the figure in 
the bills. Mr. Navroz Langrana used to ignore such blank column while sanctioning and approving the bill. 


That he reported such incidence to his senior Mr. Shantanu 5. Bhadkamka, M.D. and who directed him to 
investigate and initiate the disciplinary action against the culprit. 


That he called Mr. Javed, the supplier of the mobile phone and Mr. Javed in presence of Mr. A.K. Kunte, 
Sr. Dy. Manager admitted inflating the bills at the instance of concerned workman and Mr. Javed gave his statement 
in writing. Therefore, he on the basis of the written statement of Mr. Javed, initiated disciplinary action against 
concerned workman as per the directions of Mr. Shantanu s. Bhadkamka, M.D. and placed the workman under 
suspension on 25.02.2005. Then enquiry was started against the workman. Mr. Javed was noticed during the 
departmental enquiry but who refused to appear, rather he brought a false allegation against the company for putting 
pressure on him for giving false statement against the workman in writing. 


He has also stated at the relevant time the concerned workman was working as a Sr. Clerk in A/cs. Dept. and 
whose duty was to make entries of approved bills in books of accounts and on the basis of which payment used to be 
released after his approval. It was the duty of concerned workman to issue cheque to the parties after approval. 
Further, he during his examination in chief under oath before the tribunal he has proved the charge sheet, suspension 
order, disputed bills etc. 


However, during the cross examination he has admitted that he has not charge sheeted or brought any charge 
against the concerned workman for modification and fabrication of disputed mobile bills. Further, he has admitted 
that he acted on the report of Mr. Moghe, Dy. Manager [A/cs.] and who reported that there was alteration and 
modification in the mobile bills. But Shri Prashant Sharad Moghe in his cross examination discussed above admitted 
that he did not notice any discrepancy in the bills and did not find any discrepancy in between written figures and 
amount written in the words in those disputed bills. 


He has further admitted that Mr. Jeevan Pawar, the concerned workman has no authority to sign on the 
cheque for payment of bills. That bills are also produced before the concerned officer who signed the cheque. The 
cheque is prepared and signed after the bill is approved by the concerned officer. He has further admitted in his cross 
examination that Shri Ganesh Narayan Karandikar and Mr. Navroz Langrana were the approving and sanctioning 
authorities of those disputed bills. The concerned workman used to prepare the cheques on the basis of approved bills 


4044 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : NOVEMBER 11, 2023/KARTIKA 20, 1945 [PART II—SEC. 3(ii)] 


signed by Shri Ganesh Narayan Karandikar and Mr. Navroz Langrana. He has further admitted that he and 
Mr. Lagoo, the joint authorized signatories signed on those disputed cheques issued against disputed bills. At the 
time of signing the cheque, the amount mentioned therein was rechecked and re-verified with the relevant invoices. 


Therefore, from cross examination of this witness it is seen that Shri Ganesh Narayan Karandikar and Mr. 
Navroz Langrana were approving and sanctioning authorities of the disputed bills and not the concerned workman. 


He has further admitted during cross examination that Mr. Javed through his letters dated 05.07.2005 and 
13.07.2005 brought allegations against him for coercing him to give statement before Mr. A.K. Kunte, Sr. Dy. 
Manager on 25.02.2005, otherwise his other pending bills would be withheld. Such statement further makes the 
allegation that the concerned workman had influenced Mr. Javed, the vendor to inflate the disputed mobile bills 
appears to be doubtful. 


From the evidence of Shri Girish Achut Gadre, it appears that it is he and Mr. Lagoo were the authorized 
signatories of the cheque and not the concerned workman at the relevant time. Further, it is seen Shri Ganesh Narayan 
Karandikar and Mr. Navroz Langrana were the two officials, who were responsible to approve the bills and check the 
invoices and it was not the concerned workman. So it is not known how this concerned workman who was neither the 
approving authority of the bills nor the signatory of the cheque could manipulate the dispued bills and invoices. 


Thus, from the evidence of Shri Prashant Sharad Moghe and Shri Girish Achut Gadre, it appears that after 
the approval of bills and invoices by Shri Ganesh Narayan Karandikar and Mr. Navroz Langrana, cheque was 
prepared and signed by Shri Girish Achut Gadre and Mr. Lagoo, the joint signatories and who too before putting their 
signatures on the cheques used to verify and check the invoices. 


The management has also examined Shri Ganesh Narayan Karandikar. He in his evidence in chief on 
affidavit stated that the establishment used to buy mobile sets for official purpose from M/s. Om Sai Electronics and 
Gift Articles, Santacruz [East], Mumbai — 400 055. Mr. Javed, the Proprietor of M/s. Om Sai Electronics and Gift 
Articles, Santacruz, used to personally deliver the mobile set along with bills to him. That Mr. Javed submitted the 
bill for Rs.7150/- for the mobile set. That he took the delivery of mobile set and signed on the bill having an amount 
of Rs.7150/- and at that time Mr. Navroz Langrana was the administration in-charge was present. He never received 
or approved any bill against the said mobile phone for Rs.17150/-. Later he was enquired about the bill by Shri 
Prashant Sharad Moghe and he was shocked to find that the bill was for Rs.17,150/- instead of Rs.7150/-. 


However, during his cross examination he has stated that in the bill there is a column for writing amount in 
words or letters that he did not ask Mr. Javed to fill the said blank column and that he approved the bill leaving the 
said column blank, but at the same time he has admitted that he did mention in his report that there was alteration or 
modification in the bills and did not state that such modification and alteration was done by the concerned workman. 
He has stated it is the duty of the concerned workman to prepare cheque and present the same before the signatories 
for signatures. 


Shri Arvind Krishanji Kunte, ex-employee of the management in his evidence in chief on affidavit stated that 
in his presence Mr. Javed admitted that out of 4 bills submitted by him he has altered 2 bills bearing No. 394 and 
93EV as per the instructions of the concerned workman who was in need of money. That Mr. Javed further admitted 
that he handed over the inflated the amount of Rs.20,000/- against those two disputed bills to concerned workman 
Shri Jeevan Pawar. He has stated that he obtained the statement of Mr. Javed without any coercion and under duress. 


Surprisingly, this witness during his cross examination admitted there is line of signature of the approving 
authority on the amount written in words on those bills. So a question may arise, then how there can be manipulation 
in the column meant for writing the amount in words / letters, when the signature of approving authority appears over 
the amounts written in words. His such evidence further makes the statement given by Mr. Moghe and Mr. Gadre that 
column meant for writing the amount of bill in words were always kept blank doubtful. Further, this witness has 
admitted that Mr. Javed had filed an application alleging he had obtained his statement incriminating the concerned 
workman for inflating the bills under pressure and under coercion. 


It is very interesting to note the management for reason best known to it has failed to produce the main 
witness Mr. Javed on whose statement recorded by Mr. Kunte, the management has acted and put the concerned 
workman under suspension and thereafter charge sheeted him. In order to prove incriminatory statement given by Mr. 
Javed against the concerned workman, the management ought to have produced him and prove his incriminating 
statement given against the workman before the tribunal and which the management has failed to do so. Therefore, in 
the eyes of law the uncorroborated incriminating statement of Mr. Javed is of no value and cannot be used against the 
concerned workman. 


Further, the management for reason best known to it has failed to produce and examine Mr. Navroz 
Langrana, a vital witness to this case. 


Therefore, in view of the evidence of the above four witnesses of the management and as discussed leaves no 
room for doubt the management has failed to bring home charge of manipulation of bills and thereby 
misappropriation of Rs. 20,000/- against the concerned workman beyond preponderance of probability. 


[भाग तर---खण्ड 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : नवम्बर 11, 2023/कार्तिक 20, 1945 4045 


Infact, it appears that management of ATC (Clearing & Shipping) Pvt. Ltd. and especially Shri Girish Achut 
Gadre in order to save the high rank officers, the real culprits who were involved or indulged in the scam of looting 
the company financially by preparing inflated bills during audit appears to have made a Sr. Clerk Mr. Pawar a 
scapegoat. The concerned workman appears to have been victimized by the management and a victim of unfair labour 
practices probably to save its official namely Shri Ganesh Narayan Karandikar and Mr. Navroz Langrana, the two 
officials who were responsible in approving those disputed bills and Mr. Girish Achut Gadre and Mr. Lagoo, the two 
signatories of the cheques. 


Therefore, this tribunal holds the management has failed to prove the charge of misappropriation against the 
concerned workman beyond preponderance of probabilities. Consequentially the order of dismissal of Shri Jeevan 
Pawar, Sr. Clerk w.e.f. 21.10.2005 is held to be illegal. 


It has come on record the concerned workman was 63 years old on 06.01.2020, the day he gave evidence 
before this tribunal. Therefore, it appears he has already been superannuated from the service on his attaining the age 
of superannuation either at the age of 58 years or at the age of 60 years, whichever is applicable to him. Therefore, the 
question of his reinstatement in service does not arise, but he is entitled to get full back wages from the day he was 
placed under suspension i.e. on 25.02.2005 till his superannuation from the service. He is further entitled to get all the 
service benefits to which a retired employee of ATC (Clearing and Shipping) Pvt. Ltd. is entitled to i.e. pension, 
gratuity, leave encashment, P.F. and other statutory entitlements. 


Management of ATC (Clearing and Shipping) Pvt. Ltd. is hereby directed to pay all the entire back wages 
along with interest @ 12% p.a. along with pensionary benefits to the concerned workman within six months from the 
date hereof failing which the concerned workman shall be entitled to recover or realise the same as per rules and laws. 


Accordingly, a final award is hereby passed in favour of Shri Jeevan S. Pawar, a Sr. Clerk holding his 
termination to be illegal. Reference No. CGIT-1 / 31 of 2006 is hereby disposed of. 


Justice K. D. BHUTIA, Presiding Officer

supersession of (i) Group ‘C’ posts in the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Central Institute of Psychiatry, 
Ranchi Rules, 208 in so far as it relates to the post of Pathological Laboratory Technician; and 


(ii) the Hospital for Mental Disease Ranchi (Recruitment to Class III and Class IV posts) Rules, !959 in so 
far as it relates to the post of Senior Laboratory Technician, except as respects things done or omitted to be done 
before such supersession, the President hereby makes the following rules regulating the method of recruitment to the 
post of Medical Laboratory Technologist in the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, the Central Institute of 
Psychiatry, Ranchi, namely:- 


. Short title and commencement.- (|) These rules may be called the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, 
Central Institute of Psychiatry, Kanke, Ranchi, Medical Laboratory Technologist (Group ‘B’ Post) 
Recruitment Rules, 2023. 


(2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. 


2. Number of posts, classification and level in pay matrix.- The number of the said post, its classification and 
level in the pay matrix attached thereto, shall be as specified in columns (2) to (4) of the Schedule annexed to 
these rules. 


3. Method of recruitment, age-limit, qualifications, etc.- The method of recruitment, age-limit, qualifications and 
other matters relating to the said post shall be as specified in columns (5) to ((3) of the said Schedule. 


4. Disqualification.— No person,- 
(a) who has entered into or contracted a marriage with any person having a spouse living; or 


(b) who, having a spouse living, has entered into or contracted a marriage with any person,

other matters relating to the said posts shall be as specified in columns (5) to (/3) of the said Schedule.

law applicable to such person and the other party to the marriage and that there are other grounds for so doing, exempt 
any person from the operation of this rule.

by order, and for reasons to be recorded in writing, and in consultation with the Union Public Service Commission, 
relax any of the provisions of these rules with respect to any class or category of persons.

MINISTRY OF EARTH SCIENCES 
(India Meteorological Department) 
New Delhi, the 3rd November, 2023 


G.S.R. 6.—In exercise of the powers conferred by the proviso to article 309 of the Constitution and in 
supersession of India Meteorological Department Senior Private Secretary Recruitment Rules, 2008, India 
Meteorological Department (Private Secretary) Recruitment Rules, 2003 and Ministry of Earth Sciences (India 
Meteorological Department) Group ‘B’ and Group ‘C’ (Non-Gazetted) Ministerial (Stenographer Grade-I and Grade- 
ID) posts Recruitment Rules, 20Il, except as respects things done or omitted to be done before such supersession, the 
President hereby makes the following rules, regulating the method of recruitment to the posts of Senior Private 
Secretary, Private Secretary, Stenographer Grade-I and Stenographer Grade-II, in the Ministry of Earth Sciences, 
India Meteorological Department, namely :- 


l. Short title and commencement. - (|) These rules may be called the Ministry of Earth Sciences, India 
Meteorological Department (Stenographer Cadre posts) Recruitment Rules, 2023. 


(2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. 


2. Application. - These rules shall apply to the posts as specified in column () of Schedule annexed to these 
rules. 
3. Number of post, classification and the level in the pay matrix - The number of said post, its classification 


and level in the pay matrix attached there to shall be as specified in columns (2) to (4) of the aforesaid 
Schedule.

4. Method of Recruitment, age-limit and qualifications etc.- The method of recruitment, age-limit, 
qualifications and other matters relating to the said post shall be as specified in columns (5) to (I3) of the 
said Schedule. 

5. Disqualifications. - No person, - 


(a) who has entered into or contracted a marriage with a person having a spouse living; or 
(b) who, having a spouse living, has entered into or contracted a marriage with any person, 
shall be eligible for appointment to the said posts : 


Provided that the Central Government may, if satisfied that such a marriage is permissible under the personal 
law applicable to such person and other party to the marriage and that there are other grounds for so doing, exempt 
any person from the operation of this rule. 


6. Power to relax.-Where the Central Government is of the opinion that it is necessary or expedient so to do, it 
may, by order, for reasons to be recorded in writing and in consultation with the Union Public Service 
Commission with respect to post relating Senior Private Secretary relax any of the provisions of these rules 
with respect to any class or category or persons. 


7. Saving. - Nothing in these rules shall affect reservations, relaxation of age-limit and other concessions 
required to be provided for the Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Other backward classes, Ex-servicemen 
and other special categories of persons in accordance with the order issued by the Central Government from 
time to time in this regard.

G.S.R. 62.—In exercise of the powers conferred by the proviso to article 309 of the Constitution and in 
supersession of the Central Institute of Coastal Engineering for Fishery, Accountant (Group ‘B’ post) Recruitment 
Rules, 20!7, except as respects things done or omitted to be done before such supersession, the President hereby 
makes the following rules regulating the method of recruitment to the post of Accountant in the Central Institute of 
Coastal Engineering for Fishery, Bengaluru under the Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal 
Husbandry and Dairying, namely:- 


l. Short title and commencement. -(|) These rules may be called the Central Institute of Coastal Engineering for 
Fishery, Accountant (Group ‘B’ Post) Recruitment Rules, 2023. 


(2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. 


2. Number of post, classification and level in pay matrix.-The number of the said post, its classification and level 
in the pay matrix attached thereto shall be as specified in columns (2) to (4) of the said Schedule annexed to these 
rules. 


3. Method of recruitment, age-limit, qualifications, etc.-The method of recruitment, age-limit, qualifications and 
other matters relating to the said post shall be as specified in columns (5) to (3) of the said Schedule. 


4. Disqualification. -No person, - 
(a) who has entered into or contracted a marriage with a person — having a spouse living; or 
(b) who, having a spouse living, has entered into or contracted a marriage with any person, 
shall be eligible for appointment to the said post: 


Provided that the Central Government may, if satisfied that such marriage is permissible under the personal 
law applicable to such person and the other party to the marriage and that there are other grounds for so doing, exempt 
any person from the operation of this rule. 


5. Power to relax. -Where the Central Government is of the opinion that it is necessary or expedient so to do, it 
may, by order and for reasons to be recorded in writing and in consultation with the Union Public Service 
Commission, relax any of the provisions of these rules with respect to any class or category of persons. 


6. Saving. -Nothing in these rules shall affect reservation, relaxation of age-limit and other concessions required to 
be provided for the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes, the Other Backward Classes, the Ex-servicemen and 
other special categories of persons in accordance with the orders issued by the Central Government from time to 
time in this regard.

makes the following rules regulating the method of recruitment to the post of Deputy Commandant (Wireless) in the 
Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel National Police Academy, Hyderabad, under the Ministry of Home Affairs, namely:-

2023.

qualifications and other matters relating to the said post shall be as specified in columns (5) to (13) of the said

G.S.R. 164.—In exercise of the powers conferred by the proviso to article 309 of the Constitution, the 
President hereby makes the following rules regulating the method of recruitment to the post of Senior Scientific 
Officer in the Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel National Police Academy, Hyderabad, under the Ministry of Home Affairs, 
namely: - 


1. Short title and commencement. - (1) These rules may be called the Ministry of Home Affairs, Sardar 
Vallabhbhai Patel National Police Academy, Senior Scientific Officer Group ‘A’ post Recruitment Rules, 2023. 


(2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. 


2. Number of post, classification and level in the pay matrix. - The number of post, its classification and level 
in the pay matrix attached thereto shall be as specified in columns (2) to (4) of the Schedule annexed to these rules. 


3. Method of recruitment, age-limit, qualifications, etc.- The method of recruitment, age-limit, qualifications 
and other matters relating to the said post shall be as specified in columns (5) to (13) of the said Schedule. 


4. Disqualification. - No person, - 
(a) who has entered into or contracted a marriage with a person having a spouse living; or 
(b) who, having a spouse living, has entered into or contracted a marriage with any person, 
shall be eligible for appointment to the said post: 


Provided that the Central Government may, if satisfied that such marriage is permissible under the personal law 
applicable to such person and the other party to the marriage and that there are grounds for so doing, exempt any 
person from the operation of this rule. 


5... Power to relax.- Where the Central Government is of the opinion that it is necessary or expedient so to do, it 
may, by order and for the reasons to be recorded in writing, relax any of the provisions of these rules after consultation 
with the Union Public Service Commission with respect to any class or category of persons. 


6. | Saving.- Nothing in these rules shall affect reservation, relaxation of age-limit and other concessions required to 
be provided for the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes, the Other Backward classes, the ex-servicemen and the 
other special categories of persons, in accordance with the orders issued by the Central Government from time to time 
in this regard.

G.S.R. 167.—In exercise of the powers conferred by the proviso to article 309 of the Constitution and in 
supersession of the Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel National Police Academy, Assistant Director (Computer) and 
Programmer Recruitment Rules,1988, in so far as they relate to the post of Assistant Director (Computer), except as 
respects things done or omitted to be done before such supersession, the President hereby makes the following rules 
regulating the method of recruitment to the post of Assistant Director (Computer) in the Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel 
National Police Academy, Hyderabad, Ministry of Home Affairs, namely:- 


1. Short title and commencement. — (1) These rules may be called the Ministry of Home Affairs, Sardar 
Vallabhbhai Patel National Police Academy, Assistant Director (Computer), Group ‘A’ Post, Recruitment Rules, 
2023. 


(2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. 


2. Number of post, classification and level in pay matrix. - The number of the said post, its classification and 
level in the pay matrix attached thereto shall be as specified in columns (2) to (4) of the Schedule annexed to these 
rules. 


3. Method of recruitment, age-limit, qualifications, etc. - The method of recruitment, age-limit, qualifications 
and other matters relating to the said post shall be as specified in columns (5) to (13) of the said Schedule. 


4. Disqualification. - No person,- 
(a) who has entered into or contracted a marriage with a person having a spouse living; or 
(b) who, having a spouse living, has entered into or contracted a marriage with any person, 
shall be eligible for appointment to the said post: 


Provided that the Central Government may, if satisfied that such marriage is permissible under the personal 
law applicable to such person and the other party to the marriage and that there are other grounds for so doing, exempt 
any person from the operation of this rule. 


5. Power to relax. - Where the Central Government is of the opinion that it is necessary or expedient so to do, it 
may, by order and for reasons to be recorded in writing and in consultation with the Union Public Service 
Commission, relax any of the provisions of these rules with respect to any class or category of persons. 


6. Saving. — Nothing in these rules shall affect reservation, relaxation of age-limit and other concessions required 
to be provided for the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes, the Other Backward Classes, the Ex-servicemen and 
other special categories of persons in accordance with the orders issued by the Central Government from time to time 
in this regard.

G.S.R. 168.—In exercise of the powers conferred by the proviso to article 309 of the Constitution and in 
supersession of the Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel National Police Academy (Non- gazetted - Non-Ministerial Staff) 
Recruitment Rules, 1981, except as respects things done or omitted to be done before such supersession, the President 
hereby makes the following rules regulating the method of recruitment to the post of Staff Nurse in the Sardar 
Vallabhbhai Patel National Police Academy, Hyderabad in the Ministry of Home Affairs, namely :- 


1 Short title and commencement. - (1) These rules may be called the Ministry of Home Affairs, Sardar 
Vallabhbhai Patel National Police Academy, Hyderabad, Staff Nurse (Group ‘B’ Post) Recruitment Rules, 2023 


(2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. 


2. Number of post, classification and level in pay matrix. -The number of the said post, its classification and 
level in the pay matrix attached thereto shall be as specified in columns (2) to (4) of 116 Schedule annexed to these 
rules. 


3. Method of recruitment, age limit, qualifications, etc.- The method of recruitment, age limit, qualifications 
and other matters relating to the said post shall be as specified in columns (5) to (13) of the said Schedule. 


4. Disqualification. - No person,- 
(a) who has entered into or contracted a marriage with a person having a spouse living; or 
(b) who, having a spouse living, has entered into or contracted a marriage with any person, 
shall be eligible for appointment to the said post: 


Provided that the Central Government may, if satisfied that such marriage is permissible under the personal 
law applicable to such person and the other party to the marriage and that there are other ground, for so doing, exempt 
any person from the operation of this rule. 


5. Power to relax.- Where the Central Government is of the opinion that it is necessary or expedient so to do, it 
may, by order and for the reasons to be recorded in writing and in consultation with the Union Public Service 
Commission, relax any of the provisions of these rules with respect to any class or category of persons. 


6. Saving. — Nothing in these rules shall affect reservation, relaxation of age-limit and other concessions 
required to be provided for the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes, the Other Backward Classes, the Ex- 
servicemen and other special categories of persons in accordance with the orders issued by the Central Government 
from time to time in this regard.

G.S.R. 170.—In exercise of the powers conferred by the proviso to article 309 of the Constitution, and in 
supersession of the Bureau of Police Research and Development Staff Car Driver (Group ‘C’ post) Recruitment Rules, 
1973, except as respects things done or omitted to be done before such supersession, the President hereby makes the 
following rules regulating the method of recruitment to the posts of Staff Car Driver (Special Grade), Staff Car Driver 
(Grade-I), Staff Car Driver (Grade-II) and Staff Car Driver (Ordinary Grade) in the Bureau of Police Research and 
Development, Ministry of Home Affairs, namely: - 


1. Short title and commencement.—(1) These rules may be called the Ministry of Home Affairs, Bureau of Police 
Research and Development, Staff Car Driver (Special Grade), Staff Car Driver (Grade-I), Staff Car Driver (Grade-II) 
and Staff Car Driver (Ordinary Grade) Recruitment Rules, 2023. 


(2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. 
2. Application.-These rules shall apply to the posts specified in Column (1) of the Schedule annexed to these rules. 


3. Number of posts, classification and level in the pay matrix.-The number of said posts, their classification and 
the level in the pay matrix attached thereto, shall be as specified in Columns (2) to (4) of the said Schedules. 


4. Method of recruitment, age-limit, qualifications, etc.—The method of recruitment, age-limit, qualifications and 
other matters relating to the said posts shall be as specified in Columns (5) to (13) of the said Schedules. 


5. Disqualifications—No person,— 
(a) who has entered into or contracted a marriage with a person having a spouse living; or 
(b) who, having a spouse living, has entered into or contracted a marriage with any person, 
shall be eligible for appointment to the said posts: 


Provided that the Central Government may, if satisfied that such marriage is permissible under the personal 
law applicable to such person and the other party to the marriage and that there are other grounds for so doing exempt 
any person from the operation of this rule. 


6. Power to relax.-Where the Central Government is of opinion that it is necessary or expedient so to do, it may, by 
order and for reasons to be recorded in writing and in consultation with the Union Public Service Commission in case 
of Staff Car Driver (Special Grade), relax any of the provisions of these rules with respect to any class or category of 
persons. 


7. Saving.—Nothing in these rules shall affect reservation, relaxation of age-limit and other concessions required to be 
provided for the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes, the Other Backward Classes, ex-servicemen and other 
special categories of persons in accordance with the orders issued by the Central Government from time to time in this 
regard.

MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
(Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare) 
New Delhi, the 14th November, 2023 


G.S.R. 171.—In exercise of the powers conferred by the proviso to article 309 of the Constitution, the 
President hereby makes the following rules regulating the method of recruitment to the posts of Technical Experts in 
the National Rainfed Area Authority, Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture and 
Farmers Welfare, namely.- 


1. Short title and commencement.-(1) These rules may be called the National Rainfed Area Authority, 
(Technical Experts), Recruitment Rules, 2023. 


(2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. 


2. Number of posts, classification and level in the pay matrix.-The number of said posts, their classification 
and level in pay matrix attached thereto shall be as specified in columns (2) to (4) of the Schedule annexed to these 
10165.

3: Method of recruitment, age-limit, qualifications, etc. - The method of recruitment to the said post, age- 
limit, qualification and other matters connected therewith shall be as specified in columns (5) to (13) of the said 
Schedule. 
4. Disqualification.-No person.- 
(a) who has entered into or contracted a marriage with a person having the spouse living; 
or 

(b) who, having a spouse living, has entered into or contracted a marriage with any other person, 
shall be eligible for appointment to the said post: 

Provided that the Central Government may, if satisfied that such marriage is permissible under the personal 
law applicable to such person and other party to the marriage and that there are other grounds for so doing, exempt 
any person from the operation of this rule. 

5. Power to relax.- Where the Central Government is of the opinion that it is necessary or expedient so to do, it 
may, by order and for reasons to be recorded in writing, and in consultation with the Union Public Service 
Commission, relax any of the provision of these rules with respect to any class or category of persons. 

6. Saving.- Nothing in these rules shall affect reservations, relaxation of the age-limit and other concessions 
required to be provided for candidates belonging to the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes, ex-servicemen, Other 
Backward Classes and other special categories of persons in accordance with the orders issued by the Central 
Government from time to time in this regard.

Central Leprosy Teaching and Research Institute, Chengalpattu, namely:- 


1. Short title and commencement.-(1) These rules may be called the Ministry of Health and Family 
Welfare, Central Leprosy Teaching and Research Institute, Chengalpattu, Cobbler Grade-I (Group ‘C’ 
Post) Recruitment Rules, 2023.

(a) who has entered into or contracted a marriage with a person having a spouse living; or

personal law applicable to such person and the other party to the marriage and that there are other grounds 
for so doing, exempt any person from the operation of this rule.

do, it may, by order and for reasons to be recorded in writing, relax any of the provisions of these rules with 
respect to any class or category of persons. 


6. Saving.-Nothing in these rules shall affect reservation, relaxation of age-limit and other concessions 
required to be provided for the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes, the Other Backward Classes, the 
Ex-servicemen and other special categories of persons in accordance with the orders issued by the Central 
Government from time to time in this regard.

G.S.R.173.—In exercise of the powers conferred by the proviso to article 309 of the constitution, and in 
supersession of National Malaria Eradication Programme, Delhi Junior Translator (Hindi), Recruitment Rules, 1984 
so far as they relates to the post of Junior Translator (Hindi) except as respects things done or omitted to be done 
before such supersession, the President hereby makes the following rules regulating the method of recruitment for the 
post of Junior Translator (Hindi) in the National Center for Vector Borne Diseases Control (NCVBDC), under the 
Directorate General of Health Services, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, namely:- 


1. Short title and commencement. - 


(i) These rules may be called the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, National Centre for Vector Borne 
Disease Control, Junior Translation Officer, (Group 'B’ Post) Recruitment Rules, 2023. 

(ii) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. 

25 Number of post, classification and level in the Pay Matrix. - The number of post, its classification and the

10165. 


3: Method of Recruitment, age-limit, qualifications etc. - The method of recruitment, age-limit, qualifications 
and other matters shall be as specified in columns (5) to (13) of the said Schedule. 

4. Disqualification. - No person. - 

(i) who has entered into or contracted a marriage with any person having a spouse living, or 

(ii) who, having a spouse living, has entered into or contracted a marriage with any person, 


shall be eligible for appointment to the said post: 


Provided that the Central Government may, if satisfied that such marriage is permissible under the personal law 
applicable to such person and the other party to the marriage and that there are other grounds for so doing, exempt any 
person from the operation of this rule. 


5. Power to relax. - Where the Central Government is of the opinion that it is necessary or expedient to do so, 
by order, for reasons to be recorded in writing and in consultation with the Union Public Service Commission, relax 
any of the provisions of these rules with respect to any class or category of persons. 


6. Saving.-Nothing in these rules shall affect reservations, relaxation of age-limit and other concessions required 
to be provided for the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes, the Ex-Servicemen, the other Backward Classes, and 
other special categories of persons in accordance with the orders issued by the Central Government from time to time 
in this regard.

G.S.R. 175.—In exercise of the powers conferred by proviso to article 309 of the Constitution, and in 
supersession of the:- 


(i) Vocational Rehabilitation Centres (Group 'B' Gazetted Posts) Recruitment Rules 1996 in so far as they relate 
to the post of the Rehabilitation Officer; 


(ii) Vocational Rehabilitation Centres (Group 'B' Non-Gazetted Posts) Recruitment Rules 1996 in so far as they 
relate to the post of the Rehabilitation Counselor; and 


(ili) Vocational Rehabilitation Centres (Group 'C' and ‘D’ Posts) Recruitment Rules 1980 in so far as they relate to 
the post of the Assistant (Store), 


except as respects for things done or omitted to be done before such supersession, the President hereby makes the 
following rules regulating the method of recruitment to Group 'B' posts of Rehabilitation Officer, Rehabilitation 
Counselor & Assistant (Store) in the offices of National Career Service Centres for Differently Abled (erstwhile 
Vocational Rehabilitation Centres) under the Directorate General of Employment, Ministry of Labour and 
Employment, namely: - 


1. Short title and commencement:- 


(i) These rules may be called the National Career Service Centre for Differently Abled (Group 'B' posts) 
Recruitment Rules, 2023. 


(ii) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. 


2. Application:- These rules shall apply to the posts specified in column (1) of the Schedule annexed to these 
tules. 
3, Number of post, classification and Level in Pay Matrix:- The number of the said posts, their classification 


and the Level in the Pay Matrix attached thereto, shall be a specified in columns (2) to (4) of the said Schedule 
annexed to these rules. 


4. Method of recruitment, age limit, qualifications, etc. :- The method of recruitment, age limit, 
qualifications and other matters relating thereto, shall be as specified in columns (5) to (13) of the aforesaid Schedule. 


5. Disqualification:- No person, - 
(i) who has entered into or contracted a marriage with a person having a spouse living, or 
(ii) | who, having a spouse living, has entered into or contracted a marriage with any person, 
shall be eligible for appointment to the said posts; 


Provided that the Central Government may, if satisfied that such marriage is permissible under the personal law 
applicable to such person and the other party to the marriage and that there are other grounds for so doing, exempt 
any person from the operation of this rule.

0. In this matter, initially the petitioner/workman denied the validity and legality of the enquiry report. But, on 
20.06.209 this Tribunal has framed issues to decide the validity of domestic enquiry. Accordingly, this Tribunal has 
passed separate orders holding that the domestic enquiry is invalid on the ground that on 08.06.20I3 the petitioner 
was referred to corporate medical board and pending the examination before medical board he was been terminated 
from service. Hence, this Court is of the considerable view that though the opportunity was given to the petitioner, it 
is not full-fledged opportunity been given to him, his medical examination was pending before the medical board and

4. Here, this Tribunal relied upon a Judgment of Hon’ble Delhi High Court between Sh. Navin Chandra vs 
Union Of India (Uoi) And Others, dt.27-07-2006, wherein their lordships held that the respondents have heavily 
relied upon the judgment of the Supreme Court in the case of Controller of defense Accounts (Pension) and Ors v. 
S.Balachandran Nair to contend that the opinion of the Medical Board is final and cannot be questioned before the 
Court. The principle of law enunciated by the Supreme Court in this case is not a matter of controversy and in any 
case is binding on the Courts. Their Lordships have clearly indicated that the view expressed by the Medical Board 
has primacy and would be respected by the Courts. There can be no doubt to the proposition that for the opinion of 
the Medical Board to attain its primacy as afore-referred, it must be inconformity with the statutory provisions 
framed by the competent authorities. If a report is ex-facie not inconformity with the various regulations is not 
supported by any investigative or diagnostic evidence and is arbitrary or ex-facie perverse then it cannot be permitted 
to have the same value as indicated in the various judgments of the High Courts as well as the Supreme Court. 


l4(a). Therefore, in the present case on hand, admittedly, the respondents/ Company did not adduce any evidence 
by examining any of the doctor from medical board to show that the deceased Petitioner No.l was made fit for duty 
and the same was intimated to the deceased Petitioner No.l. Further, on the other hand even as per the evidence of 
॥५७.], he stated that according to the past record of the petitioner/workman he regularly attended the job up to 20I3 
and he further admitted that the deceased petitioner submitted an application to send him Medical board on account of 
ill-health even prior to more than two (2) years service. Therefore, it is clear that the deceased Petitioner No.l was 
suffering with ill-health during 20l3 and due to which, he failed to attend the duty. Therefore, in view of the above 
discussions, it is clear that the deceased Petitioner No.l has not attended the duty on account his ill-health since he 
was waiting for the result from medical board of the respondents company, whether he was fit or unfit to the duty. 
Moreover, dismissing the deceased Petitioner No.l from service just prior to 25 days of his retirement, which is 
nothing but unfair labour practice and victimization. 


4056 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : NOVEMBER 8, 2023/KARTIKA 27, 945 [PART II—SEC. 3(ii)] 


5. Further, the contention of the Petitioner No.l/deceased employee is that he was appointed as General 
Mazdoor in the year 98, and served the company for 33 years, this is his very |“ dismissal from service and he hails 
from a very poor family and has got no other livelihood and facing untold financial problems, hence prayed to 
consider the case under section |l-A of I.D., Act. 


6. In support of the above contentions, the learned counsel for the petitioner/workman has relied upon a 
decision of the Hon’ble High Court reported in 20I2 (!) ALD 220 (DB), wherein their lordships observed that: 


“The Industrial Disputes Act, /947 is a social welfare legislation, which required to be interpreted keeping 
in view the goals set out in the Preamble and Directive principles of State Policy in Part-IV of the 
Constitution. Merely because workman approached to Labour Court with delay, relief cannot be denied. No 
indication in the Act that delay extinguishes right conferred on the workmen under Industrial Law. The 
Labour Court is conferred with very wide discretion under section /7-4,. The Industrial Court conferred with 
very wide discretion under section 77-44 of the Act for granting appropriate relief”. 


7. Therefore, in view of the above decisions and the facts and circumstances of the case, if we come to quantum 
of sentence it is settled law that the discretion of which can be exercised under section |l-A is available only on the 
existence of certain factors like punishment being disproportionate to the gravity of misconduct so as to disturb the 
conscience of the Court, or the existence of any mitigating circumstances which require the reduction of the sentence, 
or the past conduct of the workman which may persuade the Labour Court to reduce the punishment. Therefore, in 
the present case on hand, a perusal of record, it shows that the Petitioner No.l/deceased employee served the 
company from the year 98] i.e., for 33 years and this is his very [7 dismissal from service. Further, the petitioners 
submitted that they hail from a very poor family and has got no other livelihood and facing untold financial problems, 
hence prayed to consider the case under section |l-A of I.D., Act. Moreover, there is no dispute that the petitioner 
No.I/ deceased employee has attended his duties regularly upto 20l3. Further, admittedly, there is no dispute that the 
petitioner applied for medical board on account of ill-health i.e., lower back pain and joint pain and he was forwarded 
to Dy. Chief Medical Officer, Area Hospital, vide letter, dt.08.04.20I3 marked under Ex.M-2. Hence, it can be said 
that the petitioner No.l/deceased employee is suffering from ill-health and as discussed above, the 
respondents/company failed to intimate the deceased Petitioner No.| with regard to his result of medical examination. 
Hence, in view of the above circumstances of the case as well as 33 years of service rendered by the Petitioner No. |/ 
deceased employee as well as since the respondents/company failed to intimate whether the deceased Petitioner No. | 
was made fit for duty or not, the deceased Petitioner No.! shall be treated as medically unfit for duty. Consequently, 
the LR petitioners are entitled for medical unfit benefits of deceased Petitioner No.l. Hence, this Tribunal is of the 
opinion that the punishment imposed by the respondents/company against the Petitioner No.l/deceased employee is 
illegal, hence, deserves to be set aside since the disciplinary authority cannot be permitted to act arbitrarily and work 
like a Roman Knight and it cannot be allowed a fight between David and Goliath as in the present case on hand. 


8. Therefore, in view of the above facts and circumstances and keeping in view of the principle “temper justice 
with mercy” and to meet the ends of justice, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the punishment imposed on the 
Petitioner No. l/deceased employee vide the Proceedings, dt.04..20I5 under Ex.M-2 is seti aside as illegal, hence, 
it deserves to be set aside. However, since the Petitioner No.l was dead on 2.07.209 as per Ex.W-4 and his legal 
heirs are brought on record, the relief is to be molded by this Tribunal properly and this Tribunal is of the considered 
opinion that the Petitioner No.2/Palle Ramu who is son of the deceased employee is entitled to dependant 
employment. Further, admittedly, there is no dispute that the LR petitioners are received retirement benefits of the 
Petitioner No.l/deceased employee; hence, the LR petitioners are not entitled for any benefits except dependant 
employment to the Petitioner No.2/Palle Ramu and the Petitioner No.l/ deceased employee shall be treated as 
medically unfit from service. However, the petitioners are not entitled to any back wages since the petitioners might 
have gainfully employed during pendency of this Industrial Dispute from the date of dismissal of petitioner. Hence, 
the punishment imposed by the Respondents company is hereby set aside. Accordingly, the Point No.2 & 3 are 
answered. 


9. In the result, the petition is allowed partly and the dismissal order dt.04..205 under Ex.M-I2 is hereby set 
aside. The Respondents’ company is hereby directed to provide dependant employment to the Petitioner No.2/Palle 
Ramu. However, the LR petitioners are not entitled to any back wages and any other medical unfit benefits. The 
Award shall come into force on expiry of (30) days from the date of its publication.

encashment, Bonus and Notice Pay. But no documentary evidence could be filed by any of them in support of the 
respective claims. 


4. The workmen again filed individual statement of claim revising the earlier claim vide petition dated 
3.03.2023. But, again they could not file any supporting document as evidence. 


5. Per contra the management filed reply dated 07.08.2023 that the management has not received copy of any 
claim from the workmen. However, the management has submitted their stand that their written statement and replies 
filed earlier may be looked into before passing any order. 


6. On 29.08.2023 Sri Sanjay Kumar Pandey, Sri Niranjan Kumar, Sri Ravi Kumar and Sri Prabhakar Singh, 
filed photo copies of some papers like Gate Passes as Contract Labour & temporary passes and attendance cards for 
some months. These copies of attendance cards are not authenticated by any one. 


7. The management filed petition on 4.09.2023 that the photocopy of attendance cards filed by some of the 
workmen for few months are tampered and fabricated. In support of their statement they filed attested copies of 
attendance cards issued by the management company and duly attested by the Notary. 


8. From the submissions of the workmen, revised statements, claims, revised claims and filing of petitions 
before the Asstt. Labour Commissioner (C), Patna and subsequently for adjudication by two separate Industrial 
Tribunals at Patna and Dhanbad simultaneously for the same cause, it seems that the concerned workmen are 
confused and misled lot. They could not file any single authenticated document in support of their claims as evidence. 
As thus, the claims are devoid of any authenticated evidence to be relied by this Tribunal on claims made. 


9. That the concerned workmen seemed to be misguided is also reflected through the fact that they have 
submitted claims in respect of PF, Gratuity, Bonus and minimum wages which are covered under different respective 
Acts and not in the terms of reference as per schedules of references for the concerned workers. 


20. On analysis of submissions made by both side, non filing of any evidences in support of their claim by the 
workmen concerned and copy of the attendance card duly notarized and statement filed that the photo copies of 
attendance card as filed by the workmen concerned are tampered and fabricated it is established that the workmen 
have failed to prove their claim on merit. Further the industrial dispute raised by the concerned workmen before the 
Presiding Officer, Industrial Tribunal, Patna on same matters of dispute and award passed in that Reference ID Case 
No. 0I (C) of 205 between Sri Sanjay Kumar Pandey and 8 others with notification issued by Government of India 
on 6.02.20l6 as ‘NO DISPUTE AWARD” on the ground of having no claim and evidence in respect of the claim 
made by the petitioners. 


2i. Considering the above findings this Tribunal is of the opinion that the workmen concerned in the reference 
cases as recorded above are not entitled for any relief on the claim made by each of them. As such award is passed 
with no relief. 


[भाग Il—ave 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : नवम्बर 8, 2023/कार्तिक 27, 945 4065 


22. Summing up the entire findings and discussions it is found that the workmen could not produce any 
authenticated document in respect of their appointment, number of days worked/months worked during entire period 
of service as claimed and date of termination/retrenchment and so this Tribunal is unable to consider any 
compensation even as per Section 25F of the I.D. Act, !947 as claimed and prayed by the workmen concerned. 


23. At the same time it is also observed that the management could not maintain transparency in dealing with 
engagement of the workers on contract. Had the management maintained transparency and explained the workers full 
facts of contract and disengagement the workmen might not have taken the route for litigation. 


24. Considering the long follow up with the Tribunal workmen may be allowed some relief as part of legal 
expenses made, as compensation at the rate of Rs. !0,000/- each. The management should pay Rs. 0,000/- each to 
the concerned workers under the noted references as per this award within 60 days of receipt of notification on 
publishing this award by the Government of India in Official Gazette, after due verification and authentication of the 
workmen concerned and to the legal heir in reference to the workman Sir Binod Sah who has been reported to have 
died on 25.06.20I5 for which the management has objected on the substitution by his widow Smt. Indu Devi as no
